results.title: DOCKER-USER chain state
results.subject: host
results.message: DOCKER-USER exists with no filtering rules: published ports are not filtered by the host firewall

fix.hint: No direct fix: filter published ports in DOCKER-USER (ufw-docker does this) or publish them on 127.0.0.1 only.

results.title: Provider firewall (outside view)
results.subject: host
results.message: the provider firewall cannot be seen from inside the host; run `stackward probe` from another machine to see what is reachable

fix.hint: Add a provider network firewall that allows only the ports your ingress needs

results.title: Published container ports do not bypass the host firewall
results.subject: container:coolify/coolify
results.message: coolify is reachable from anywhere past the host firewall: 0.0.0.0:8000->8080/tcp: DOCKER-USER has no filtering rules, and UFW's input rules do not apply to published ports

fix.hint: Publish on 127.0.0.1 (127.0.0.1:5432:5432) or the tailnet address, or put the service behind the reverse proxy instead of publishing it. To keep a wildcard binding, filter it in DOCKER-USER (for example drop new connections on the public interface except from allowed sources), or install ufw-docker and open it with a route rule for the sources that need it.

results.title: No container mounts the Docker socket
results.subject: container:coolify-proxy
results.message: coolify-proxy mounts the Docker socket (/var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro); expected for a proxy, but it is root on the host if compromised; a read only mount does not stop connecting to a socket; managed by Coolify as its proxy: expected, a platform default the panel does not let you change

fix.hint: Remove the socket mount. If the container needs to read Docker state, put a socket proxy in front (for example tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy with only CONTAINERS=1) and point the container at it.

results.title: No host network, PID or IPC namespace
results.subject: container:tunnel/cloudflared
results.message: tunnel-1 uses the host network (worst of 2 replicas)

fix.hint: Use a bridge network and publish only the ports needed (on 127.0.0.1 behind the proxy); remove pid: host and ipc: host.
